text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading share index ended a four-day losing streak, rebounding 1.6 percent following a solid recovery on Wall Street, dealers and strategists said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4914.2, up 79.2 points, or 1.64 percent.

FRANKFURT - Germany's IBIS DAX index ended electronic dealings 2.69 percent ahead, after a strong afternoon performance on Wall Street gains and a more stable dollar lifted the market. The DAX-30 index closed at 4169.62, up 91.02 points, or 2.23 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4190.45, up 109.90 points, or 2.69 percent.

PARIS - French shares closed 1.77 percent down on Monday after having lost more than 3.3 percent earlier in the day on the back of a big slide on Wall Street on Friday when Paris was closed. The CAC-40 index closed at 2936.16, up 66.03 points, or 2.30 percent.

ZURICH - Swiss shares recovered from losses the day before, gaining more than three percent on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI). The Swiss market index closed at 5580.1, up 174.5 points, or 3.23 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks turned tail after a morning rally and closed lower, with shares of leading blue-chip companies weighed down by persistent worries over Japan's feeble economic recovery, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 18961.00, down 80.10 points, or 0.42 percent.

HONG KONG - Concerns about a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar rocked the territory's share prices with interest rate sensitive property and banking stocks suffering heavy losses as interbank rates jumped. The Hang Seng index closed at 15477.26, down 619.62 points, or 3.85 percent.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market trod a wary path to a slightly firmer finish with one eye on Wall Street and a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting and the other on local annual corporate report cards. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2620.9, up 2.4 points, or 0.09 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares held gains achieved by noon to close up as Wall Street opened firmer, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7397.2, up 35.9 points, or 0.49 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1017.6, up 0.9 points, or 0.09 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9086.4, up 37.4 points, or 0.41 percent.
